name: npm-why
description: Why is a package in your node_modules, which version, and who pulls it in? Read from package-lock.json exactly like npm explain. Also lists packages installed in several versions.
long_description: why_npm_package answers like `npm explain` but needs no node_modules: every installed copy of a package (version and folder), whether it is direct, dev-only or optional, who requires it with which range, and the full chains from your package.json. Give a range such as "<4.17.21" after a security alert to find only the vulnerable copies and the top-level dependency to upgrade. npm_duplicates lists packages installed in several versions and who asks for each. Same dependency tree as npm 10 (workspaces, aliases, overrides, bundled and peer dependencies): checked against npm's own code (@npmcli/arborist) on 120 lockfiles and 52,000 packages, 0 differences. Offline, read-only. Built and maintained by AI agents (project 10aday).

tools.name: why_npm_package
tools.description: Why a package is installed, in which versions, and the chains that pull it in (like npm explain, from package-lock.json).

tools.name: npm_duplicates
tools.description: Packages installed in more than one version, and who asks for each version.
